newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: HOWARD SAYS GIVE POLICIES A CHANCE
The Prime Minister, John Howard, says while he is very unhappy about the unemployment rate, he's urged people not to pass judgement until the Government's policies have had a chance to flow through.
Howard says the Government does take responsiblity for a rise in the jobless rate to 8.8 percent.
The Prime Minister has told ABC TV's 7-30 Report, he's confident Government policies and a pick up in the economy will see a much stronger jobs market next year.
The rise in unemployment was unexpected.
It has prompted calls for another cut in interest rates and more Government action in areas such as industrial relations reform.
DOWNER TO ATTEND ALL CEREMONIES IN HONG KONG
Foreign Minister Alexander Downer will attend all the ceremonies marking the hand-over of Hong Kong to China later this month.
The Prime Minister, John Howard, says Mr Downer will attend the swearing in of Hong Kong's provisional legislature.
That's despite pressure from the Opposition parties and a boycott by Britain and the United States.
Howard says he doesn't deny China is an undemocratic nation, but human rights issues are best pursued through dialogue.
He says it's to Australia's advantage to have a close economic relationship, and an honest political relationship with China.
OBSTACLES FOR VISITORS FROM JAPAN
A Japanese tourism official says tour prices and visa restrictions are among the reasons fewer Japanese people are visiting Australia.
Growth in Australia's top overseas market has been falling since October.
Hiroyuki Imoto from the Japanese Travel Bureau told a Melbourne tourism conference Australia should reduce tour prices and ease visa restrictions.
He has also criticised the lack of direct flights from Osaka to Cairns, saying the JTB has no motivation to continue promoting Cairns as a destination.
Imoto has also urged the New South Wales Government to reconsider its proposed 10% Sydney bed tax.
He says the tax will add to the cost of tour prices and will be a disincentive to Japanese travellers.
Howard says he hasn't gone overboard about a special relationship with China.
But he says more can be done on human rights through a dialogue than by voting for resolutions in the United Nations.
BORBIDGE CRITICISES ABC'S SATELLITE TV SERVICE

The Queensland Premier says the ABC has done more damage to Australia's reputation in Asia than the views of Pauline Hanson. Rob Borbidge is currently in Indonesia with a Queensland business delegation.
He says what he has seen on the ABC's Satellite service, Australia-TV, has been a string of negative stories about Australia being pumped into a major market.
He cites stories about the Stolen Children, reported problems in orphanages, and comments on Aboriginal Affairs by the New South Wales Premier and the Governor General.
Borbidge wants ABC management to review the news and current affairs going into Asia, which he says is making it hard to sell Australia in the region.
INDUSTRY WARNS GOVERNMENT ON UNEMPLOYMENT
Manufacturers have cast doubt on the Prime Minister's claim that employment will pick up next year, saying a recovery in their industry could take much longer.
The Chamber of Manufactures says there's now no sign of the confidence its members had when the Government came into power, that there would be change.
Chamber director, Barry Watchorn, says that confidence has not turned into a reality.
Watchorn told ABC Radio the Government will need to do more than rely on further interest rate cuts and reform in industrial relations and taxation.
He says a coherent industry policy is needed for investment confidence.
ANNUAL CONFERENCE OF NSW NATIONAL PARTY
The Wik decision, tariff policy and the constitutional convention are set to be key areas of debate at the New South Wales National Party's annual conference which begins in Sydney today.
Federal National Party leader, Tim Fischer, officially opens the conference this morning.
It's expected the Party will reaffirm its hardline stance that pastoral leases extinguish native title.
The Federal Government's industry policy will be debated with one proposal for a uniform rate on tariff protection for all industries.
There'll also be debate on the republic issue following the Government's appointment of veteran National Party MP Ian Sinclair to chair the Constitutional Convention in December.
The conference will also see the chairmanship of the party handed over to a woman, for the first time, with Helen Dickie voted into the position yesterday.
